security_spec.violation_condition: QEMU TCG's IMSIC MMIO write handler (riscv_imsic_write) processes MSI writes synchronously: the pending bit is set atomically and the external interrupt line is raised inline before the MMIO write returns. Because QEMU's device model serializes all MMIO/DMA operations on the BQL (Big QEMU Lock) or per-device iothread, a device MSI write to IMSIC will always appear to complete before any subsequent DMA read from the same device, thereby implicitly providing the load-acquire ordering that the spec (PR #118) intentionally removed. Guest drivers that incorrectly rely on MSI acting as a read barrier will work on QEMU but fail on real RISC-V hardware.
security_spec.vulnerability_pattern: riscv_imsic_write.*qatomic_or.*eistate.*IMSIC_EISTATE_PENDING; synchronous MSI delivery without deferred/batched interrupt injection; IMSIC MMIO write processed inline on BQL before device DMA read completion dispatch
security_spec.summary: QEMU's synchronous IMSIC MSI write handling implicitly enforces load-acquire ordering (interrupt observed before subsequent device reads) that the spec intentionally removed, masking guest driver race conditions on real hardware

findings.finding: QEMU's IMSIC MMIO write handler processes MSI writes synchronously on the BQL: the pending bit is set atomically (qatomic_or) and the external interrupt line is raised inline (qemu_irq_raise via riscv_imsic_update) before the MMIO write returns. Because QEMU serializes all device MMIO/DMA operations under the BQL, a device MSI write to IMSIC will always appear to complete before any subsequent DMA read from the same device, thereby implicitly providing load-acquire ordering that the RISC-V AIA spec (PR #118) intentionally removed. Guest drivers developed on QEMU that incorrectly rely on MSI acting as a read barrier will function correctly on QEMU but will fail on real RISC-V hardware where the device may read stale data after MSI delivery. This is a fidelity gap in the emulation model, not a code correctness bug — QEMU's synchronous device model inherently provides stronger ordering than real hardware.

riscv_imsic_update correctly implements IMSIC interrupt evaluation: lowering the line, checking eidelivery and topei for pending+enabled interrupts, and raising the line if any exist. Atomic operations on eistate are correct for concurrent CSR and MSI access. The enpend flag at eistate[base] correctly tracks whether the external IRQ line is currently asserted. Functionally correct per the AIA specification.

CSR RMW path correctly dispatches to the appropriate handler based on ISELECT register encoding. Page selection logic correctly handles M-mode (page 0 only), S-mode with virtualization (vgein-based page selection with bounds check), and S-mode without virtualization (page 0). All handlers (eidelivery, eithreshold, topei, eip, eie) correctly call riscv_imsic_update after modification.
